marks.gloss_en: דתני רב אושעיא כוותיה: אבר הפורש ממנה כפורש מן החי ... ואסור לבני נח
מסייע ליה לרב אידי בר אבין
one who wants to be healthy cuts an olive-bulk of flesh from the place of slaughter, salts it very well, rinses it very well, and waits until its soul departs; gentile and Jew alike are permitted it
הואיל ויכול לגוררה ולהעמידה על פחות מכזית (= p_chiz_yachol_legorera)
Chizkiya: since he can chop it and reduce it to less than an olive-bulk [hechsher is needed]
R' Yirmeya to R' Zeira: did Chizkiya say so? but it was stated: two simanim cut and still twitching -- Chizkiya: no [law of] limbs, [for] it is dead
two simanim or most of two cut, and it is still twitching -- Chizkiya: it is not [subject to the law of] limbs
יצתה מכלל חיה, ולכלל מתה לא באת (= p_zeira_yatzta_michlal_chaya)
R' Zeira [for Chizkiya]: it has left the category of the living and has not entered the category of the dead
R' Yosei: because it will end up imparting severe impurity
Chizkiya's 'no limbs': it is dead
a Jew who slaughtered a non-kosher animal for a gentile, two simanim or most of two, and it twitches -- it imparts food impurity
a limb separating from it is as one separating from the living, flesh separating from it as flesh separating from the living, and it is forbidden to the sons of Noach, even after its soul departs
one siman or most of one cut -- it does not impart food impurity; stabbed -- it has no impurity at all
a gentile who slaughtered a kosher animal for a Jew, and it twitches -- it imparts food impurity, but not carcass impurity
[the gentile's case] a limb or flesh separating from it is as separating from the living, forbidden to the sons of Noach even after its soul departs
[the gentile's case] one siman or most of one -- no food impurity; stabbed -- no impurity at all
a gentile cut where it does not render it tereifa, and a Jew came and completed it -- it is kosher
a Jew cut, whether where it renders it tereifa or not, and a gentile came and completed the slaughter -- it is invalid

one who wants to eat from an animal before its soul departs cuts an olive-bulk of flesh from the place of slaughter, salts it very well, rinses it very well, waits until its soul departs, and eats it; gentile and Jew alike are permitted it
R' Elazar: if he paused in it, pressed in it -- what [is the law]?
thus said R' Yochanan: it requires valid slaughter as a kosher animal
R' Zeira: does it save the swallowed items inside it?
Rav Sheshet: it imparts food impurity -- and it saves?! [it does not save]
Abaye: one who lies with it is liable, for it does not impart carcass impurity
Rav Huna: and that is when he collected it
Rav Huna: two half-olive-bulks [of carcass flesh] on the hide -- the hide nullifies them
